title: Rendezvous spill-tiering and cross-stage KV shadowing for multi-GPU pipeline
creator: Evan Park
description:
Problem: On cross-split (tensor + pipeline) models we observe poor GPU memory packing for KV caches: hotspots in a few devices, high memcpy/spill rates, and increased tail latency during synchronous continuous-batching windows. This ticket proposes a rendezvous-based spill-tiering allocator and a lightweight cross-stage KV shadowing protocol to improve memory balance, reduce runtime spills to host, and preserve cache locality for in-flight streaming requests.

Proposal summary:
- Use a rendezvous hashing mapping to assign KV keys (microshard ids derived from sequence id + head sharding) to a primary GPU owner and a ranked spill order of candidate devices.
- Implement a two-tier residency model: "hot-local" (fast KV directly in GPU local slab with lease ownership) and "warm-remote" (read-only shadow slices kept as pinned peer memory or cached on neighboring devices).
- Add an async prefetcher at pipeline stage boundaries: when the coordinator predicts next-stage consumption, it initiates background KV fetch into local slab using the rendezvous ranking to choose the lowest-cost candidate.
- Introduce a lease-based eviction handshake at pipeline micro-boundaries to avoid double-writes and to enable fast failure-safe handoff when pipeline parallel stage moves ownership mid-request.
- Integrate with continuous batching controller so prefetch windows align with current batching latency SLO and do not increase tail latency beyond threshold.

Why different from prior work: existing sharding efforts focus on static stripe or slab allocation; this ticket focuses on dynamic ranked spill candidate selection (rendezvous) combined with a shadowing mechanism across pipeline stages to minimize synchronous host spills and accelerate warm-up of KV during streaming workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end 95th percentile token latency for streaming workloads does not regress by more than 5% under typical continuous-batching profiles
Host spill volume (GB/hour) from KV caches reduced by at least 60% on 8xA100-like topologies compared to current baseline
Peak device memory imbalance (max_used - median_used) reduced by >= 35% across the GPU pool during mixed-length sequence workloads
Eviction/lease protocol yields no correctness regressions in >1000 synthetic regression tests and validated against existing KV integrity checks
Automated e2e benchmark reproducible (link in links) and perf dashboard updated with experiment IDs

decisions: Use rendezvous hashing for stable ranked candidate lists to minimize remapping churn when devices join/leave
Lease-based ownership instead of exclusive locks: leases are short (100-500ms) with renewal at pipeline boundaries to reduce stall risk
Shadow slices will be read-only and maintained as pinned peer memory when topology supports NVLink; otherwise pinned host fallback
Async prefetch triggered at pipeline stage boundaries must be budgeted against continuous-batching windows; default budget set to 15% of batch latency SLO
Fallback policy: if a rendezvous candidate is overloaded, fall back to next-ranked candidate and increment per-key metric for adaptive remapping tuning
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Rendezvous ranking computation adds CPU overhead under very high QPS. Mitigation: cache rank lists per microshard and use vectorized ranking; add adaptive caching TTL based on access frequency.
Risk: Lease renewal storms if many requests contest the same keys. Mitigation: jittered renewals and randomized lease backoff; add per-key contention backpressure to batching controller.

Risk: Peer-memory fallback on non-uniform topologies increases latency variance. Mitigation: annotate topology costs and prefer low-latency candidates; expose topology-aware policy for Dedicated customers.
Risk: Complexity in correctness across pipeline stage ownership transfers. Mitigation: comprehensive fuzz tests + invariants in KV integrity checker; manual runbook for rollback (link in links).
